ai.title: Add bun status-services command to check dev service health
ai.summary: New scripts/status-services.ts implements `bun status-services` to verify running state of db, studio, sdk, and web. Checks Docker container status for `manicode-db`, queries `lsof` for web/studio ports, reads PIDs from `debug/console/services.json`, and hits `/api/healthz`. Registered in package.json scripts and documented in knowledge.md alongside existing start/stop commands.

eli5.text: You can now ask your computer to tell you whether your project's helper programs, the database, the admin screen, the toolkits, and the website preview, are actually running, just by typing a single check command. Instead of guessing from error messages or opening a bunch of windows to see what's alive, the command quietly pings each piece and reports which ones are connected and which ones are missing. The same list you already use to start or close down those helpers now includes a quick status option.

ai.title: SDK release 0.10.2 ships native tool calls and bundled agents
ai.summary: Bumped @codebuff/sdk from 0.10.1 to 0.10.2 in sdk/package.json (the version field only; the diff is a one-line change with no source files modified in this commit). This release bundles the preceding 0.10.x work already documented in the SDK CHANGELOG, including native tool calls under the hood (0.10.0), more reliable tool calls (0.10.1), JSON Schema serialization of custom tool inputs via z.toJSONSchema for JSON transport survival, type export fixes, and the consolidated `bun run verify` SDK build/lint path used by sdk-release.yml. The SDK package continues to expose the public client library surface in sdk/src/index.ts while treating @codebuff/common, @codebuff/agent-runtime, and @codebuff/code-map as externals for dts-bundle-generator.
ai.evidence: Single-line bump in sdk/package.json changing version from "0.10.1" to "0.10.2"; no source diff visible beyond package.json. Analysis notes classify this commit as a release-bump and cite "Bump SDK version to 0.10.2". The 0.10.2 release updates list enumerates user-visible features, model changes, and CLI improvements shipped in this release (e.g. native tool calls in 0.10.0, more reliable tool calls in 0.10.1, and the bundled 0.10.2 release updates above).

eli5.text: This release adds native tool calls to the SDK and bundles ready-to-use AI agents directly into the Freebucks CLI binary. You can now use new agent modes (default, max, plan, lite) via slash commands or flags, and the CLI auto-shows your usage balance when credits run low. Images can be attached through /image or clipboard paste, and the CLI remembers your last agent mode in new sessions. Improvements include click-to-position cursor in multiline input, mouse-click suggestion menus, and a simplified single-command dev setup. The context pruner now preserves tool-call pairs and accounts for system prompt tokens, preventing API errors during long conversations. The slash command menu executes selections directly, and the publish command shows a visual checklist of agents to upload.

ai.title: CLI message pagination added
ai.summary: CLI chat now uses message pagination to improve performance with long conversations. A `LoadPreviousButton` component is added to `cli/src/components/load-previous-button.tsx`, and `cli/src/chat.tsx` implements state for `visibleMessageCount` and `hiddenMessageCount` to slice messages. The default batch size is 15 messages.

eli5.text: When you have a long chat with the assistant in the terminal, the conversation now loads in batches of 15 messages at a time instead of all at once. A new 'Load previous messages' button appears above the visible messages, which you can click to bring in older parts of the conversation one batch at a time. This makes the chat faster and more responsive when you've been talking for a while, and prevents the terminal from slowing down or freezing with very long histories.

ai.title: CLI batched message updater with guaranteed cleanup
ai.summary: CLI streaming now uses createBatchedMessageUpdater, queuing AI message updates and flushing them at a 100ms interval via setInterval. This reduces state churn during rapid token streams. The updater exposes flush and dispose methods, with dispose called in a finally block in use-send-message.ts to guarantee interval cleanup even if completion or error handlers throw. Post-dispose updates fall back to immediate application.

eli5.text: When the assistant is typing out a response one word at a time, it now groups small updates together and applies them roughly ten times per second instead of updating the screen with every single letter. This keeps the display from flickering or stuttering during fast streams, and if anything goes wrong while the response finishes, the system still automatically cleans up the background timer so it doesn't keep running. You won't see a new button, but the chat display should feel smoother and steadier when messages appear quickly.

ai.title: Fix custom option selection in CLI ask-user form
ai.summary: Selecting the custom option in the CLI ask-user form now explicitly clears `selectedIndex` and `selectedIndices`. The `accordion-question.tsx` component updates the custom option symbol to use checkbox styling for multi-select questions. This resolves state conflicts when toggling between predefined choices and custom text input.

eli5.text: When you use the command-line assistant and choose the "Custom" option to type your own answer (instead of picking from the suggested choices), the menu now correctly shows that choice as selected using checkbox or radio-button styling, matching how the other options look. This fixes a glitch where switching back to the suggested choices could leave the menu in a confused state. If you use the command-line version of the assistant and pick a question that lets you type your own answer, you'll see the highlight update properly now.

ai.title: CLI: set followup prompt to input instead of sending
ai.summary: Followup prompts now populate the input field via `setInputValue` instead of auto-submitting with `onSubmitPrompt`. This allows users to review and edit suggestions before execution. Clicked items remain interactive for re-selection, and terminal width checks prevent layout overflow on narrow screens.

eli5.text: When you click a suggested follow-up question in the CLI chat, it now appears in the input box for you to review and edit before you send it, rather than being sent immediately. You'll also notice that clicked follow-up items stay interactive so you can re-select them again, and the suggestion descriptions now only appear on terminals that are at least 80 characters wide to prevent layout overflow on narrower screens. This affects anyone using the CLI chat feature with suggested follow-up prompts.

eli5.text: The assistant can no longer run untrusted JavaScript in a locked-down QuickJS sandbox; the underlying engine and its configuration options (memory limits, stack size, interrupt handling) have been deleted entirely. ai.title: Add env dependency injection architecture
ai.summary: New env dependency injection architecture replaces direct process.env access with typed getters (getCliEnv, getBaseEnv) across CLI, SDK, and Common. This enables explicit environment mocking in tests and strict type safety for terminal/IDE detection vars. Scope covers cli/src/utils/env.ts, common/src/env-process.ts, and sdk/src/env.ts. Key detail: CliEnv type extends BaseEnv with specific vars like KITTY_WINDOW_ID, VSCODE_PID, and CODEBUFF_IS_BINARY for precise binary/dev mode branching.

eli5.text: The program now reads its settings through a single, organized system instead of grabbing each value piecemeal from the background. This lets the team test features in a controlled way and stop crashes caused by typos or missing values. Right now, this rewrite touches how the CLI spots whether you run it in a terminal or through an app, picks your default editor, and decides if it should use a special fast file-search tool. Most people won't notice anything new today because the visible behavior stays the same, but the program becomes more reliable and easier to maintain.

ai.title: Fix drizzle-kit env loading via bunx --bun
ai.summary: Switched `db:generate`, `db:migrate`, and `db:studio` scripts in `packages/internal/package.json` to use `bunx --bun drizzle-kit`. This forces execution via Bun runtime, ensuring `.env.local` variables like `DATABASE_URL` load correctly, as Node.js does not auto-load these files. Consequently, the `clear_inherited_env_vars` function and `CODEBUFF_SKIP_ENV_CLEAR` flag were removed from `.bin/bun`, `scripts/dev.ts`, and `scripts/start-services.ts`. New internal documentation in `packages/internal/knowledge.md` details this requirement for future database scripts.

eli5.text: Internal database tools now run through Bun's runtime so they can read your local environment settings automatically, preventing connection errors that happened when they used the default tool runtime. This only affects engineers running database migration or administration commands, and there is nothing you need to do differently. The change is live today.
